epay.text: Any employer who is required to remit wage withholding tax on a weekly basis is required to remit payment via electronic funds transfer (EFT).

deposits.interpretation: Colorado sets a filing and remittance frequency from the employer's ANNUAL Colorado income tax withholding: quarterly under $7,000; monthly at least $7,000 but not more than $50,000; weekly $50,000 or more. The guide states $50,000 in both the monthly and the weekly row; this profile treats exactly $50,000 as monthly (the 'not more than' row) and flags the overlap here. The frequency is first set from the estimate on the employer's withholding account application, and the Department raises it on January 1 if actual withholding for a year exceeded the estimate, so the frequency is an INPUT (what the Department assigned) or is derived from a supplied annual liability. Weekly: the Saturday-to-Friday week, due the 3rd business day after the Friday; the final weekly period of the year ends December 31 whatever weekday it is (due the 3rd business day after December 31), and a week is NOT split at quarter ends. Monthly: the 15th of the following month. Quarterly: the last day of the month after the quarter. Each return covers wages PAID in the period. Due dates falling on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday move to the next business day. An EFT payment satisfies both filing and payment, so no separate return is made.

returns.name: Colorado W-2 Wage Withholding Tax Return (DR 1094)
contents: Monthly and quarterly filers (not weekly filers) must file a return for each period even if no tax is due; the due date follows the filing frequency (quarterly shown; monthly the 15th of the next month).
An employer who remits by EFT does not file a separate return: the EFT satisfies both payment and filing.
A paper return is only for employers not required to remit by EFT.

returns.name: Annual Transmittal of State W-2 Forms (DR 1093)
contents: Copies of every W-2 go to the employee and to the Department no later than January 31 of the following year.
Employers who file W-2s electronically (Revenue Online) do not submit a paper DR 1093 except to remit additional tax or claim a refund.
An overpayment not deducted from a later period in the same year is claimed on the DR 1093 filed before January 31, or later by a Claim for Refund (DR 0137).

returns.name: Quarterly wage detail report and premium payment
contents: Quarterly wage detail reports, monthly employment data and premium payments are due the last day of the month after the quarter: April 30, July 31, October 31 and January 31.
If the date is a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday the payment is timely on the next business day (CDLE FAQ; the FAQ states it for the premium payment).
Premium owed at the June 30 annual computation date carries a penalty of the past-due amount or 1% of taxable payroll, whichever is less, billed in four quarterly installments.
